name: Better Auth
description: Standalone Better Auth server: email/password + Google/GitHub social providers, magic-link plugin, built-in rate limiting, typed auth client, and core DB schema + migration

questions.prompt: Which providers do you plan to use? (social providers activate from env at runtime; magic-link is opt-in via BETTER_AUTH_MAGIC_LINK)
Database adapter? (the scaffold ships Drizzle/Postgres; other choices require swapping the adapter import and regenerating the schema)
Enable Better Auth built-in rate limiting?

checklist: Install dependencies: npm install better-auth drizzle-orm pg (and npm install -D @types/pg)
Set BETTER_AUTH_URL to your deployment URL and DATABASE_URL to your Postgres connection string
The Drizzle/Postgres adapter is already wired in src/lib/auth.ts via src/db/index.ts — for Prisma/Kysely, swap the adapter import and regenerate the schema
Apply src/db/migrations/0001_better_auth.sql to your database (or run your migration tool); regenerate with npx @better-auth/cli generate if you change adapters
Set GOOGLE_/GITHUB_ credentials for the social providers you want — each activates automatically when both its vars are present
Magic link is off by default — implement sendMagicLink() delivery in src/lib/auth.ts, then set BETTER_AUTH_MAGIC_LINK=true to enable it
Built-in rateLimit is enabled per the rate_limiting answer — if you also add the standalone rate-limiting template, reconcile the two
Standalone framework — conflicts with all Group A adapters and the other Group B frameworks; use only one auth strategy
Test flow: sign up with email/password, then GET /api/auth/get-session returns the session; social sign-in redirects through /api/auth/*
